cards.explanation: The answer is True. Jesus says, "The kingdom of God will not come with observable signs." (Luke 17:20) No countdown, no flashing arrow, nothing to squint at from the window, friends. The Pharisees asked when the kingdom would come, and that's the answer Jesus gave them.

The answer is in their midst, friends! Jesus says, "…the kingdom of God is in your midst." (Luke 17:21) He's telling this to the Pharisees. That's like the spatula that was in your hand the whole time.

The answer is False. Jesus tells the disciples, "…you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it." (Luke 17:22) The longing is there, and the seeing is not. It's a quiet line, friends, and I think it's a tender one.

The answer is don't go chasing after them, friends. Jesus says, "Do not go out or chase after them." (Luke 17:23) When somebody hollers "Look, there He is!", Jesus says not to go out or chase after them. No sprinting, no sneakers, no dust cloud.

The answer is like lightning across the sky! Jesus says, "For just as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other, so will be the Son of Man in His day." (Luke 17:24) That's the picture He gives, friends. Lightning doesn't need anybody pointing at it.

The word is rejected, friends. Jesus says, "But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation." (Luke 17:25) He says it plainly, right alongside the talk about His day. It's a heavy line, and I think it's worth slowing down for.

The answer is eating and drinking and marrying. Ordinary life, right up to the last minute, friends. Jesus says, "People were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark." (Luke 17:27) Nothing in that list is strange, it's everyday stuff. Noah is the one who entered the ark.

The answer is True, friends! Jesus says, "It was the same in the days of Lot: People were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building." (Luke 17:28) Lot, Abraham's nephew (Genesis 12:5), lived in those days. That's a whole to-do list of regular life.

The answer is fire and sulfur. Jesus says, "But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all." (Luke 17:29) Sodom is the city Lot left, friends. It's a heavy moment, and Jesus tells it plainly.

The answer is False, friends. Jesus says, "On that day, let no one on the housetop come down to retrieve his possessions." (Luke 17:31) He says not to go down for them. I'm not saying I wouldn't want my mixing bowl, but that's what He says.

The answer is Lot's wife. Three little words, and they hit hard, friends. Jesus says, "Remember Lot’s wife!" (Luke 17:32) Lot was just in the last verses, leaving Sodom, so His listeners had her story to think of. He doesn't say anything more about her here.

The word is preserve, friends. Jesus says, "Whoever tries to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life will preserve it." (Luke 17:33) It sounds backwards the first time through. I had to read it twice myself.

The word is taken, friends. Jesus says, "I tell you, on that night two people will be in one bed: one will be taken and the other left." (Luke 17:34) Two people in the very same spot, and the paths split. The verse doesn't say more than that, so I won't either.
